content.content:
features — read the commitment oxxwkrvo's own node document records about what the README's features section describes — its stated content and the rationale that explains it — and fail with a finding that names the part at issue and, where a prerequisite bears on it, the prerequisite it fails against. The check applies to the decision node alone: the README artifact the section will eventually be written into is not its subject.

LICENCE AGAINST THE NAMED PREREQUISITES. Every claim the node's commitment makes must be permitted by at least one of the eleven prerequisites this check depends on, and no part may contradict, negate, narrow away, replace or add to what the prerequisite that records that capability states.

(1) Graph, drawing and node label: every claim about the interactive graph the viewer presents, how nodes and edges are drawn, and what each node's box displays as its label must be permitted by uprztqnr, rtlotqvy and qpsnwxlu. Describing the graph surface in user-facing terms (such as an interactive graph in a panel, without naming the HTML page or webview implementation mechanism) is licensed by uprztqnr. A claim that a node's box displays anything other than its label from the jj change description — such as a visible node id or a secondary label on the box — is not licensed by qpsnwxlu and is a finding.

(2) Search interaction: every claim about finding nodes by a text query — pressing '/' with no modifier to open a focused search field without changing the current selection, pan or zoom, matching nodes whose id, label or content contains the query case-insensitively and marking none when the query is empty, stepping to the next and previous marked node with Enter and Shift+Enter in graph order with wrap-around, and pressing Esc to close the field and clear the search marks and selection — must be permitted by ksoupzqm, nvxuyzot, oovzklpv, yqwsztww and kstrrnyt. Describing the Enter and Shift+Enter traversal in user-facing terms as moving through matching nodes in graph order and wrapping at either end, without reciting the internal layout tie-break formula, is licensed by yqwsztww.

(3) Detail fields and content display: every claim about the detail panel's presentation of the selected node's Kind, Content and Rationale as three labelled sections in that fixed order (including empty sections remaining present with their labels) must be permitted by vqwoptmu, and every claim about how the Content section formats the selected node's content according to its type and whether the body is inline or in referenced files must be permitted by qwzwpxws. Describing the Content section's display in user-facing terms — prose shown as wrapped running text, structured or code content and any other content types shown verbatim in a monospaced block labelled with the content type without refusing or hiding unrecognised types, and file-referenced content showing the content type together with the referenced file paths — without reciting internal schema property names or the full internal token list is licensed by qwzwpxws.

(4) Relationships: every claim about the selected node's relationship sections — the four labelled sections 'depends_on', 'evaluates', 'dependents' and 'evaluators' listing related node ids for the selected node's prerequisites, the nodes it evaluates, the nodes that depend on it and the evaluations that evaluate it, with empty sections remaining present with an explicit empty state — must be permitted by rmovtvkt together with the parent-to-child directions mkyoyqvt and mnovnnot fix. Describing what each of the four sections lists in user-facing terms (prerequisites, evaluated nodes, dependents and evaluators) rather than raw JSON field-lookup mechanics is licensed by rmovtvkt.

(5) Closed capability licence: every claim the commitment makes about what the viewer offers must be permitted by at least one of the eleven prerequisites, and any claim none of the eleven licenses is a finding naming the claim and the prerequisite set that does not permit it. In particular, installation or marketplace instructions, a further top-level feature beyond the graph, search and detail panel, node-file schema or invalid-node warning behaviour, section collapse, placement of the search field or relationship sections on the page or relative to Kind, Content and Rationale, match highlight styling, reload behaviour, alternative search opening or dismissal, how a listed relationship id's own node content is rendered, a visible node id or secondary label on a box, or a fifth edge type or reversed relationship direction is a finding.

SUBJECT FLOOR AND USER-FACING PRESENTATION.

(6) Subject floor: across its stated commitment and rationale, oxxwkrvo must cover all five user-visible feature areas that the eleven prerequisites record — (a) the interactive graph, its box/rounded-box and solid/dashed-edge visual grammar with child-end arrowheads and visibly marked unresolved edges, and node labels from jj change descriptions (uprztqnr, rtlotqvy, qpsnwxlu); (b) the text search interaction of '/' to open without disturbing selection, pan or zoom, case-insensitive matching on node id, label or content with an empty query marking nothing, Enter and Shift+Enter stepping through marked nodes in graph order, and Esc closing the field and clearing marks and selection (ksoupzqm, nvxuyzot, oovzklpv, yqwsztww, kstrrnyt); (c) the detail panel's three labelled sections Kind, Content and Rationale in order (vqwoptmu); (d) the Content section's type-based display of running prose versus a verbatim monospaced block labelled with the content type, including unrecognised types and file paths when content lives in referenced files (qwzwpxws); and (e) the four labelled relationship sections ('depends_on', 'evaluates', 'dependents', 'evaluators') listing related node ids for prerequisites, evaluated nodes, dependents and evaluators, with empty sections still shown (rmovtvkt). A placeholder node, or a commitment that omits or defers any of these five areas, leaves that part of the use with no subject and is a finding naming the omitted area.

(7) User-facing presentation: because oxxwkrvo commits to what the README's features section presents to users, its stated commitment (content.content) must describe these features in user-facing terms rather than reciting internal node-JSON schema property names, internal schema token rosters or implementation mechanics as user prose. Fail with a finding naming the offending element if oxxwkrvo's stated commitment commits the features section to: dotted node-JSON property names or raw schema-field literals such as 'content.type', 'content.ref' or '"inline"' (for example 'as content.type spells it' or 'when content.ref is a list of repo-relative paths rather than "inline"'); enumerating the internal content.type token roster ('text, ears and review-criteria', 'visual-spec, json-schema, test and rust') as a schema-mapping specification; framing the viewer's graph surface in webview implementation mechanics ('an interactive HTML page in a webview panel'); reciting the internal layout sort tie-breaking formula ('by topological depth from the roots, then initial left-to-right position, then node id'); or stating relationship sections in terms of raw JSON field-lookup and edge-inversion mechanics ('the ids its depends_on names', 'read the same depends_on and evaluates edges from the other end'). Naming the user-visible detail-panel section labels themselves ('Kind', 'Content', 'Rationale', 'depends_on', 'evaluates', 'dependents', 'evaluators'), or explaining in content.rationale how the user-facing commitment is grounded in the eleven prerequisites, is permitted.

HOW THE CHECK IS APPLIED. Read oxxwkrvo's decision node against the eleven prerequisites; nothing runs. The check demands no particular wording, sentence count, order or layout, and fails only when one of the five feature areas in (6) is omitted or deferred, when the stated commitment violates the user-facing presentation requirement in (7), or when the node makes a claim that contradicts or overreaches the eleven prerequisites under (1)-(5).
content.rationale: The dependent is a commitment in words — the README's features section describes the viewer's graph, search, detail fields, content display and relationships in user-facing terms — so it is natural-layer, and the commitment is what the decision node's own document records, not the README artifact where the section is eventually written; that artifact is nsyxzxzr's ref, the composition below the dependent, held by its own decision and its own unit. uprztqnr, ksoupzqm, vqwoptmu, qwzwpxws and rmovtvkt are inline prose; qpsnwxlu, nvxuyzot, oovzklpv, yqwsztww and kstrrnyt are inline EARS requirement sentences, structured parents to a natural child; and rtlotqvy refs src/webview/render.ts and src/styles/grammar.css, a code parent to a natural child. Natural-to-natural edges take the eval-matrix's gate cell; the structured and code parents are unknown cells that take the gate form and are flagged for a matrix entry. One criterion covers the whole fan-out because the node's use of all eleven is one use: the features section summarises what the viewer presents across all eleven prerequisites for a user reading the README. This amendment replaces the earlier criterion because the earlier gate required oxxwkrvo to recite internal node-schema property names (content.type, content.ref, "inline"), the exact internal schema type-token roster, HTML webview hosting mechanics, internal layout sort tie-break rules and raw JSON edge-lookup phrasing as mandatory parts of the features commitment, which prevented oxxwkrvo from describing the viewer's capabilities in user-facing terms and accepted implementation-jargon prose. The amended gate licenses user-facing descriptions of all eleven prerequisites' capabilities, keeps the closed capability licence and five-area subject floor grounded in the eleven prerequisites without demanding internal schema tokens or tie-break formulas, and requires oxxwkrvo's stated commitment to present those capabilities in user-facing terms rather than leaking internal schema property names or implementation mechanics. The check is applied by reading the decision node against each prerequisite in turn; nothing runs.
